mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and increasing the present value of future cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below the 50th percentile of its historical range.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:US unemployment rate rose to 6.1% in February 2020
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a contraction in consumer spending across multiple sectors, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline from prior month
evidence_refs: fact:US retail sales and housing starts declined in February 2020
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS and HOUST both decline from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates a supply shock that disrupts production and increases uncertainty, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in a supply shock regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 235 indicates elevated inflation that triggers monetary tightening expectations, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 235.

mechanism_narrative: A GDP level below 16000 billion (GDPC1 < 16000) in a recessionary regime indicates a significant economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 < 16000.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing output and supply chain stability, supporting corporate earnings growth and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a sharp contraction in the labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise from prior month
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS and UNRATE both deteriorated in February 2020
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month.
